parole.significato: A freshwater turtle of the eastern United States of the genus Pseudemys.
parole.testo: Borrowed from Gullah cootuh (“turtle”), from an African language, e.g. Bambara kuta (“turtle”). Attested in English from the 19th century.

parole.significato: To play dance music, or to dance, in a juke.
parole.testo: From Gullah juke, jook, joog (“wicked, disorderly”) (compare Wolof and Bambara dzug (“unsavory”)).

parole.significato: Used to evoke spiritual unity and interpersonal harmony, with varying degrees of sincerity or sarcasm, as referring to…
parole.testo: From Gullah. Apparently a corruption of the English phrase “come by here” in a spiritual song.

parole.significato: A peanut, the nut-like pod containing the edible seed(s) of a leguminous plant.
parole.testo: Via Gullah from Kongo mpinda (“peanut”), also borrowed in Dutch as pinda.
